newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - slow start to the new year.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - slow start to the new year.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market was sluggish this week, with few spot sales noted, as prompt supplies remained hard to come by, traders said.
"Spots are very limited," one dealer said. "No one is bringing coffee into the U.S. unsold."

An unexpected drop in coffee stocks housed in U.S warehouses certified against CSCE futures underscored nearby supply woes, he said. The exchange reported certified coffee stocks fell by 1,607 60-kg bags in the week ended January 3, to 32,458 bags. No stocks were pending grading or recertification.
Although roasters needed to buy coffee to keep up with consumption and replenish stocks, traders said buying interest was tempered by rising futures prices and firm differentials.

News Tuesday the Brazil's government said it was working with a range of between 18.5 and 19.5 million 60-kg bags for the 1997/98 coffee crop, down from 25 million bags in 1996/97 drove the CSCE March futures to seven-month highs.

Traders said a decline in next season's arabica output, coupled with growing consumption in producing countries, would likely keep stock levels low through the second half of the year and may force roasters to switch their buying strategy.
